name: 22658-streamchat-llama31-8b-1gpu
model: NousResearch/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct -- an ungated re-upload of `meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct` under the Llama 3.1 Community License; config.json matches field for field. ~15 GiB of bf16 weights.
hardware: 1x NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3, one node, one GPU.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=512, warmup the first 15%, bounded at 4096 requests with a 1800 s safety cap.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, single turn, sent to `/v1/chat/completions` with streaming on, prompts ~192 tokens (stdev 24, clamped 128-256) and generations pinned at exactly 512 tokens. `ignore_eos: true` and `temperature: 0.0` ride in the request body, seed 42; `stream-interval` is the release default of 1, so a client receives one chunk per generated token.
purpose: A streaming chat assistant on one H100, serving 512 concurrent users short prompts and 512-token replies.
launch:
# One H100 serving a small dense model to 512 streaming chat clients at a time.
# Flat `key: value` only. A nested block is DROPPED by the flat parser, and the engine then
# runs without the option this file declares.

model-path: NousResearch/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct

tp-size: 1

# Prompt max 256 + output 512 is 768 tokens, so nothing is ever truncated.
context-length: 2048

mem-fraction-static: 0.85

# The release's own H100 default is 256, BELOW the 512 requests this setup keeps in flight, so
# the decode steps would run outside a captured graph. Costs ~1 GiB of graph buffers.
cuda-graph-max-bs: 512

chunked-prefill-size: 4096

# Not a tuning choice: on this driver and wheel set the piecewise-cudagraph warmup raises
# `CUDA error: an illegal memory access` inside `warmup_compile` before the server ever
# answers a request.
disable-piecewise-cuda-graph: true

random-seed: 42
